Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Honolulu HI
831 PM HST Wed Jul 22 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
Moderate to breezy trade winds will strengthen through the week 
and deliver periodic showers to windward and mountain areas. 

&&

.SHORT TERM UPDATE...
Isolated to scattered showers continue over windward and mauka
locations this evening, and is expected to continue through the
night. Light precipitation amounts are forecast due to
increasingly stable air moving into the state from the east. Trade
winds will increase slightly tonight and remain stronger through
at least Thursday night. All this is handled well by the current
forecast and no update is needed at this time.

&&

.PREV DISCUSSION...
Issued at 411 PM HST Wed Jul 22 2026
Radar and satellite imagery show drier air gradually filtering 
across the state from east to west this afternoon, with the 
greatest focus over Kauai. In fact, Kauai has been the main focus 
for rainfall across the state in the short term, with 12-hour 
rainfall totals ranging generally between 1 and almost 5 inches 
across the typical wetter areas. 

High pressure to the far northeast will gradually move 
southwestward over the next couple of days and strengthen. This 
will allow the moderate to breezy trades felt across the state 
today to strengthen over the second half of the week. Minor
batches of moisture will filter in on the trade wind flow, 
bringing periodic upticks in windward and mauka showers through 
the weekend, particularly during the overnight to early morning 
hours.

Next week, the weather across the state will depend on the
eventual track and intensity of Tropical Cyclone Fausto. The
National Hurricane Center is forecasting a gradual weakening of
this system as it tracks westward and enters into the Central
Pacific this weekend, with further weakening expected early next
week as it moves into a more hostile environment with cooler
waters and increased shear. At this time, its too early to
predict any direct impacts from Fausto on Hawaii, though
confidence is increasing in east-facing shores receiving a decent
swell late this weekend into early next week. See the marine
discussion below for more details. 

&&

.AVIATION...
A strengthening high pressure system north of the Hawaiian Islands
will increase trade winds with wind speeds peaking by Thursday
afternoon. A band of unsettled clouds are riding into the islands
on the trade winds tonight. Expect brief MVFR conditions mainly 
along windward mountain slopes through the early morning hours. 
Weather conditions will show improving trends after 9 AM HST.

AIRMET Sierra for mountain obscuration was expanded tonight to 
include both Kauai and the Big Island. These conditions will
likely diminish shortly after sunrise.

AIRMET Tango remains in effect for low level turbulence driven by
the strengthening trade winds.


&&

.MARINE...
High pressure far north of the state will maintain fresh to 
locally strong trades through the weekend, for which a Small Craft
Advisory (SCA) remains in effect for the typical windier channels
and waters around Maui and the Big Island. Trades are expected to
strengthen another notch Thursday into Friday, which has prompted
an expansion of the SCA to all Hawaiian Waters for Thursday and 
Thursday night. Widespread fresh to strong winds are expected 
during this time with near gales possible for the windier waters 
around Maui County and the Big Island. The strong high to the 
north is expected to eventually shift westward and weaken some, 
which should allow the trade winds to weaken a notch around 
Sunday evening. Trends in the strength and direction of winds 
early next week become less clear as a result of the uncertain 
track of a weakening Hurricane Fausto (forecast to become a 
tropical storm by Monday) in the central Pacific.

Offshore and nearshore buoys are showing an increase in energy 
over 20 second periods as forerunners from the next notable 
incoming south swell slowly fill in tonight. A High Surf Advisory 
(HSA) has been issued from 6 am Thursday as surf is expected to 
increase to advisory levels through the day. There is also 
potential to approach warning levels late Thursday into Friday as 
the swell peaks. Over the weekend, reinforcing long-period energy 
may allow advisory level surf to persist and may require an 
extension of the HSA.

Surf along east-facing shores will remain slightly below seasonal 
levels through the evening due to the weaker trades upstream of 
the islands. The Hilo buoy continues to show a small, medium-
period east swell this evening, which was likely generated by 
former TC Elida. Stronger trade winds will also support an 
increase of short-period energy heading into Thursday and Friday.
This weekend, larger surf generated by Hurricane Fausto is 
possible and could bring advisory level surf along east facing 
shores by late Sunday into early next week. 

Surf along north-facing shores will remain at flat to tiny levels
through the weekend.


&&
